steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Definition: An article is written for publication in a newspaper, magazine, or online platform. It informs, persuades, or entertains a specific audience while following journalistic conventions. | Headline Techniques: Use alliteration: "Baking Ban Begins" Ask a question: "Is This the End of Free Speech?" Make a bold statement: "Our Schools Are Failing" Use a pun or wordplay: "Storm Brewing Over Tea Tax" Create intrigue: "The Hidden Danger in Your Home" | Opening Techniques: Start with a dramatic statement Use a rhetorical question Begin with an interesting fact or statistic Open with a brief anecdote or scenario | Top Tip: Articles are meant to be read quickly. Use short paragraphs, clear topic sentences, and subheadings to guide the reader through your argument.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Write three different headlines for an article about school uniform using different techniques. | What is the "inverted pyramid" structure and when would you use it? | Write an opening paragraph for an opinion article about social media.

steps.title: Homework & Consolidation
steps.body: Consolidation, retrieval on Headline Techniques, Opening Techniques, Top Tip, and one past-paper question.
